stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A capacitor stores electric charge on two plates. Close the switch $K$ to start charging. Sweep $C$ and $U$, and complete one full charge (watch $u_C \to U$) to advance.
stages.concept: Charge stored: $Q = C \cdot u_C$. When the capacitor is fully charged, $u_C \to U$ so $Q_{max} = C \cdot U$. Energy stored: $E_e = \tfrac{1}{2}\,C\,u_C^2$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Match the target plateau: your curve must level off at $Q^{*}$. Tune $C$ and $U$ so the product $C \cdot U$ equals $Q^{*}$ within $\pm 5\%$.
stages.concept: The plateau of $q(t)$ is $Q_{max} = C \cdot U$. Many $(C, U)$ pairs reach the same $Q_{max}$ — success only depends on the product.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Only the target curve is shown. Read $Q^{*}$ from its plateau, pick $C$ and $U$ so that $C \cdot U = Q^{*}$, then press RUN. Your curve appears on submit — match $Q_{max}$ to within $\pm 3\%$.
stages.concept: The target's flat asymptote is $Q^{*}$. Read it off the y-axis, then choose any $(C, U)$ with $C \cdot U = Q^{*}$. Example: $Q^{*} = 3.0\,\text{mC}$ → $C = 500\,\mu\text{F},\ U = 6\,\text{V}$ or $C = 300\,\mu\text{F},\ U = 10\,\text{V}$.

labels.peek_hint: the curve levels off at Q_max = C·U — read Q* from the plateau on the y-axis, then pick C and U with C·U = Q*
labels.tip1: close K, watch q(t) fill toward Q_max = C·U, then sweep C and U
labels.tip2: adjust C and U so your curve's plateau lines up with the orange Q* line
labels.tip3: read Q* off the plateau of the target curve, then set C·U = Q* and press RUN

1.1: Click K to close the switch. The capacitor charges: q(t) rises toward Q_max = C·U.
1.2: Try doubling C — the plateau doubles. Try doubling U — the plateau also doubles. The product C·U is what sets the plateau.
1.3: Full charge means u_C reaches 99% of U (a few time constants). The plateau of q(t) sits at Q_max = C·U.

2.1: Compute Q_max = C·U. Adjust C and U until Q_max equals the target Q*.
2.2: Doubling C and halving U keeps Q_max the same — the plateau won't move. Any (C, U) with C·U = Q* works.
2.3: Fine-tune the C slider once you're close; small C changes = small Q_max changes at fixed U.

3.1: On the target curve, find the y-value the curve flattens to — that is Q*.
3.2: Once you know Q*, pick a round U (say 6 V) and set C = Q* / U.
3.3: Press Peek for a reading-method hint. Then set C·U = Q* and press RUN.
